Below 50% is where efficacy drops off rapidly. 70% is the one you want. While 90% and higher is actually less effective.

Isopropyl alcohol kills cells by denaturing and coagulating proteins. Purified water acts as a catalyst and aids in the alcohol penetrating the cell wall. It also increases contact time, allowing for more complete coagulation of the proteins.

In 90% concentrations or higher, not only does the alcohol evaporate quickly (reducing contact time), it causes proteins to coagulate nearly instantly on the outside (i.e. the cell wall). This has the effect of creating a protective barrier that stops further coagulation of the proteins inside the cell.

If you use Staphylococcus Aureus as an example, even a 50% solution applied to a surface will kill it within 10 seconds. However, after two hours, a 90% solution will still be ineffective.

tl;dr - Isopropyl alcohol in a 70% solution is the sweet spot for disinfecting.
